The core `OrderSetService.saveOrderSet` is called from the REST module in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, not from `openmrs-core` itself. Three production methods call it, all in the 1.12 resource implementations under `/ws/rest/v1`:

1. **`OrderSetResource1_12.save(OrderSet)`** (lines 57-72) is the main path. It resolves member concepts and order types by UUID, then calls `Context.getOrderSetService().saveOrderSet(orderSet)` at line 71. It backs the `/orderset` resource (annotation at line 38), so any create or update of an order set goes through it.
2. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.save(OrderSetMember)`** (lines 162-168) adds the member to its parent order set and saves the parent at line 166.
3. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.delete(...)`** (lines 150-155) retires the member on its parent and saves the parent at line 154.
4. **`OrderSetMemberResource1_12.purge(...)`** (lines 170-175) removes the member from its parent and saves the parent at line 174.

Items 2-4 are the member resource's write paths. Any change to `saveOrderSet` behaviour (validation, cascading, retirement, exceptions) would reach the REST API through these methods and the generic framework calls that invoke them.

Test code that depends on the same behaviour:
- `OrderSetMemberController1_12Test.shouldShowAllOrderSetMembersForAnOrderSet` (line 85, inside the method starting at line 80) saves an order set directly.

Core-side references (`OrderSetServiceImpl`, `OrderSetDAO` Javadoc, and `OrderSetServiceTest`) are not part of the REST module, so I left them out. I did not check whether the REST module has any other way to reach the service without the `saveOrderSet(` call pattern. The grep covered the whole module for that call.
